rules.rule: Check for causes of decreased consciousness
rules.problem: Mostly faithful. The page says 'Check ... pupils' with an 'Unequal or respond poorly to light' branch (raise head, discuss urgently with the referral centre), but that finding isn't checked for anywhere. It's acceptable only because no rule consumes it, so the page's pupil check is only partly encoded. Allergen exposures drop the 'past few hours' window.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis with sudden decreased consciousness
rules.problem: Structure (sudden decreased consciousness AND any of the listed features/exposures) and 'possible' match 'check for anaphylaxis'. The only gap is the footnote timing on exposures, which makes 'Exposure to Food' almost always true.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable shock with decreased consciousness and glucose ≥ 11.1
rules.problem: The page's comma list 'If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, weakness, shock likely' is encoded as a plain or, so glucose ≥ 11.1 plus weakness alone (or pulse 100 alone) gives probable shock, which leads to a 20 mL/kg bolus. It's ambiguous whether the page means any one sign or the cluster; a plain or is the most permissive reading and should be confirmed with the clinical lead (any2 or and are the alternatives). Placement inside the glucose ≥ 11.1 branch is correct.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible meningitis with decreased consciousness and temperature ≥ 38
Diagnose probable drug overdose with decreased consciousness and dilated pupils
rules.problem: Matches 'Both equally dilated → Stimulant or other drug overdose likely'. Overdose is_a Poisoning in SNOMED, so it's consistent with the separate poisoning rule.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable poisoning with decreased consciousness
rules.problem: The and/or structure follows the flowchart: the Poisoning likely bar is fed by both pinpoint sub-boxes and by the dilated/overdose box. RR < 12 is correctly scoped to the pinpoint branch only.

The header 'Give urgent attention to the patient with decreased consciousness' has no 'and any of', so the complaint alone → Urgent is justified. Not encoded: the bottom escalation (BP < 90/60, pulse > 100 or < 50, RR > 20 or < 9, SpO2 < 94%, drop in GCS → reassess ABC ⮌16), which the house briefing cites as an Emergency-level example. It's a monitoring step, so leaving it out is defensible.

summary: Most consequential: the probable shock rule treats the page's comma list (SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, RR > 30, weakness) as a plain or, so glucose ≥ 11.1 plus weakness or tachycardia alone gives probable shock. That's the most permissive reading of an ambiguous line and needs confirming. The anaphylaxis exposures (medication, food, insect bite/sting) drop footnote 1's 'within the past few hours' window. Every other condition, threshold, likely/possible mapping and the pupil flowchart structure faithfully follows the page. All SNOMED concepts exist.
